source_caption:
Some movies hit you in the gut. Atonement hits you in the heart, tears it apart, then leaves you alone with the pieces. Because Atonement (2007) lures you in with sweeping romance, then rips the floor out from under you and leaves you gasping at the screen, wondering what the hell just happened to your heart. The plot? Can't say too much. Honestly, the less you know, the better.

James McAvoy delivers a career-defining performance as Robbie. A man caught in the wrong place at the wrong time with the wrong last name. His chemistry with Keira Knightley (as Cecilia) is off the charts. The unspoken tension between them. The sheer ache of what could've been. Keira Knightley is at her best here. Forget the pirate corsets, this is her most refined, restrained, and raw performance. But the real surprise? Saoirse Ronan. As the 13-year-old Briony, she carries the weight of the entire plot on her tiny steely shoulders.
